title: Open-Ended Video Game Glitch Detection with Agentic Reasoning and Temporal Grounding

problems.name: Dataset, Benchmark, and Evaluation Mismatch
problems.evidence_sentence: While these settings provide testbeds for studying glitch understanding, they address only restricted aspects of the problem and fall short of the richer contextual analysis in real-world gameplay-based QA.

problems.name: LLM Temporal Reasoning and Time Output Instability
problems.evidence_sentence: Open-Ended Video Game Glitch Detection with Agentic Reasoning and Temporal Grounding Open-ended video game glitch detection aims to identify glitches in gameplay videos, describe them in natural language, and localize when they occur.

problems.name: Spatio-Temporal and Object/Event-Level Grounding
problems.evidence_sentence: For example, an object such as “a boat flying through the sky” may indicate a physics failure in one game, but could be a perfectly valid event in another game with stylized or fantastical mechanics.

methods.name: Benchmark or Dataset Construction
methods.evidence_sentence: To support this task, we introduce VideoGlitchBench, the first benchmark for open-ended video game glitch detection with temporal localization.

methods.name: Object/Event/Spatio-Temporal Modules

methods.name: Contrastive or Cross-Modal Alignment
